output.title: Spot vendor price changes before they hit cash flow
output.body:
If you run a small business, vendor pricing changes are one of those quiet problems that only show up after the invoice lands. The bounded workflow decision is simple: are you checking for changes early, or are you finding them late and doing the math by hand? That is the point where a small automation may help.

The fit is narrow. It makes sense when pricing notices, renewal emails, or invoice details arrive in digital text form and you already keep a baseline rate to compare against. It is less useful if the only source is scanned paperwork, because OCR and PDF scan handling are not part of our current scope. In that case, manual spot-checks may honestly be enough. No need to build a robot for a once-a-quarter shrug.

The control stays with you. A detection step can flag a change when the amount or rate moves past a defined threshold, but the owner still decides what happens next: accept it, question it, or renegotiate. No payment or contract change should happen without human approval.

A practical next step is to ask three things: how often do key vendors send price updates, in what format do they arrive, and do you already track the baseline rates you expect to pay? If the answer is unclear, start there. That tells you whether this is a real workflow to automate or just another spreadsheet wearing a cape.
